invariants: campaign is a versioned aggregate with member, stage, owner and status history

list rows, detail, membership and report requests share one content-addressed lifecycle snapshot bound to the PostgreSQL aggregate revision, authoritative member count and last event plus the ClickHouse campaign fact watermark

detail and membership reads reject a stale optional snapshot_id with CAMPAIGN_SNAPSHOT_CONFLICT, and every UI mutation carries the currently displayed snapshot_id while compatibility callers may omit it during rollout
every aggregate mutation uses stable idempotency and optimistic revision
when CAMPAIGN_AGGREGATE_V2_ENABLED is false every mutating action fails closed with 503 and no legacy business mutation is executed

when the aggregate is enabled a compatibility caller missing idempotency, expected revision or reason is normalized explicitly, records compatibility_mode in result, event and audit, and receives the generated idempotency key in the response
membership link and unlink atomically update the relation and campaign aggregate
membership is bidirectionally queryable from one repeatable-read PostgreSQL snapshot
merge locks source and target aggregates in lexical campaign-id order and atomically closes the source, transfers its authoritative members and records one immutable manifest
a merged source campaign cannot accept later aggregate or membership commands and returns its target campaign identifier
historical membership backfill is manifest-bound and resumable per campaign, binds only linked revision-zero rows, inserts missing rows and never resurrects an explicit unlink
report accepted freezes one typed PostgreSQL snapshot and never claims an object exists before its manifest commits

a leased executor renders JSON, PDF and DOCX from the same frozen model, uploads a deterministic MinIO key and atomically commits report terminal state, action job, aggregate history, outbox and audit
download is tenant and campaign scoped and verifies size and sha256 against the PostgreSQL object manifest before returning bytes
SOAR request, approval, executor and compensation states are separate; the original requester cannot approve execution or compensation
SOAR provider calls use the stable job_id as the idempotency identity and execute outside the PostgreSQL transaction under a recoverable lease
SOAR completed, partial, failed and compensated states require an immutable provider receipt; HTTP 2xx without a provider receipt never proves an external effect
SOAR terminal receipt, workflow state, campaign action job, aggregate revision, history, outbox and audit commit in one serializable PostgreSQL transaction
ClickHouse, OpenSearch and NebulaGraph acknowledge independently and the inbox is applied only after all three target watermarks commit
a lower projection revision is superseded, while a same-revision event or projection hash mismatch is an identity collision and never reaches an external target
target replay uses deterministic projection bytes and may reset one target without rewriting already acknowledged targets
domain.compensation: append an inverse versioned command when the action catalog permits it

data.target_projection_identity: tenant_id + length-delimited projection_key; immutable event rows use tenant_id + stream + event_id

negative_tests: SOAR compensation without a proven external-effect receipt is rejected
SOAR provider success without a durable receipt is rejected

journeys: SOAR independent approval, provider receipt and compensation
stop_conditions: member counts diverge or action queue budget is exceeded

tests: G1 state machine, default-off mutation rejection and compatibility metadata normalization
G2 real PostgreSQL atomic state, history, audit, outbox, idempotency replay, compatibility propagation, lease, retry, collision, tenant isolation and target rebuild
G3 one real Kafka event and trace reconciled through PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, OpenSearch and NebulaGraph
evidence: same campaign revision across list, detail, membership, report, audit and projection
same lifecycle snapshot_id across the selected list row, detail, membership and report source_snapshot_id; a changed lifecycle returns 409 rather than silently mixing versions
same snapshot sha256 across accepted command, artifact model, PostgreSQL manifest and completion event
immutable source manifest, per-campaign receipt and per-alert inserted/bound/unchanged/skipped outcome reconcile exactly
one immutable event document hash and independent applied watermark for each of clickhouse, opensearch and nebulagraph

prerequisites: PostgreSQL target worker migration and ClickHouse shadow table exist
NebulaGraph space, entity tag and relation edge accept deterministic tenant-scoped writes
all three target readiness checks pass before the worker starts
report-artifacts bucket and lifecycle exist and S3 credentials are injected
campaign SOAR provider URL and token are injected only when a verified provider is available
current image bound to evidence manifest
